correctness.rationale: For the exact printed polynomial vector field, define F=w-(b/4)(x+z). Differentiation yields xdot+zdot=1-4y, so LF=wdot-(b/4)(xdot+zdot)=-by-(b/4)(1-4y)=-b/4 identically for all real a,b and states; independently verified by symbolic coefficient cancellation. Thus along EVERY classical solution on its existence interval F(t)=F(0)-bt/4. For b≠0 a forward-complete bounded state cannot exist because F is a continuous affine state function. Any compact positively invariant set would contain a bounded forward-complete solution; any periodic orbit/compact attractor is impossible. For compactly supported invariant probability measure the integral of F would equal its translate by -bt/4 for all t, contradiction. No proof of global existence, and b=0 is excluded: (-1,1/4,±1,0) are exact equilibria when b=0. The source vector field and all seven source blobs are checked against their pinned identities; a complete Git tree was independently reconstructed.

value.rationale: Though a short affine cancellation, the result is a substantive structural correction for a specifically published and subsequently reused dynamical model: it rules out the original paper’s claimed compact hidden/coexisting attractors for ALL nonzero-b parameters, not just one numerical simulation. Negative divergence and absence of equilibria do not establish this obstruction. Future dynamical studies of this exact flow need to know it before relying on attractor or stationary-measure assumptions. The result is not a general theory of Sprott systems; its precise model-validation motivation makes the exact boundary meaningful.

limitations: Printed 2021 autonomous ODE only, b nonzero; a arbitrary; no assertion of forward completeness for all initial data.
b=0 has equilibria; do not transfer to changed 2022 fourth equation or controlled/forced network systems.
